diagnosis.summary: The operator is a tiny (32x256, 32 KB) memory-bound elementwise chain; latency is dominated by per-call launch/dispatch overhead, not math. Baseline naive_v0 = 15.36us for 5 launches (~3.1us/launch); candidate-01 removed the redundant clone and preallocated the output (11.168us for 4 launches, ~2.8us/launch). Since the arithmetic already needs 4 distinct kernels eagerly (mul + add(alpha) + sub + relu cannot be fused into fewer standard ATen ops without a compiler), further gains must come from removing launch overhead rather than kernel count. Note: the stated 99.9999% target (~15.36us -> <1.6e-5us) is not physically reachable for any real GPU kernel; the goal here is a genuine, bounded reduction in measured p50.
bottlenecks: per-launch CPU dispatch/launch cost x4 on a shared GPU
Python-level op dispatch overhead per eager op
no launch-count reduction available from ATen algebra (min 4 kernels)

candidateEvaluations.title: Replay the 4-launch affine+relu chain as one captured CUDA graph after a capture threshold
candidateEvaluations.hypothesis: If per-call launch overhead (~2.8us x 4) dominates the 11.168us measured for candidate-01, collapsing the four identical-shape kernels into a single graph replay on the benchmark's repeated same-pointer calls should cut p50 substantially while producing bit-identical results.
candidateEvaluations.change: Added _affine_relu_into/_affine_relu helpers (out = empty_like(x); mul(out=) -> add_(alpha=0.75) -> sub_(0.125) -> relu_()), a pointer/shape/dtype/device-keyed cache, and a _CAPTURE_AFTER=3 threshold: the first calls for a key run eager, only the 3rd+ call on the same key captures a CUDA graph (side-stream warmup, then torch.cuda.graph) and thereafter returns the graph's static output after graph.replay(). Capture exceptions are caught and permanently demote that key to eager; non-CUDA inputs and cache overflow also fall back to eager. get_inputs/get_test_cases/get_benchmark_inputs/reference are byte-for-byte unchanged.
